correctness.rationale: Recursive many-one degrees split into the two singleton trivial degrees and one nontrivial recursive degree. Richter--Stephan--Zhang prove that the latter contains exactly three finite-one degrees and that every many-one degree contains at most countably many. Cintioli's Corollary 7 proves that every nonrecursive many-one degree contains either one or infinitely many finite-one degrees. Hence the only cardinalities are 1, 3, and countable infinity.

evidence: Cintioli states that every nonrecursive many-one degree contains exactly one or infinitely many finite-one degrees.
Richter--Stephan--Zhang state that every many-one degree contains at most countably many finite-one degrees and that the greatest recursive many-one degree contains exactly three.
Richter--Stephan--Zhang explicitly list other finite numbers as open before Cintioli's later resolution.

value.rationale: Richter--Stephan--Zhang made the possible finite cardinalities an explicit open question. Cintioli's later theorem closes the nonrecursive case. Combining it with the exactly-three recursive exception gives the complete global cardinality spectrum and shows that three is the unique finite nontrivial value.
